steps.text: Heat a heavy skillet over medium heat. Place dried guajillo chiles into the skillet and cook, turning occasionally, until the color changes and chiles have puffed, about 5 minutes. Set chiles aside to cool for a moment. Meanwhile, toast cumin and cloves in the hot skillet until cumin seeds begin to pop; remove from the pan and set aside. Remove and discard stems, seeds, and veins of chiles, and place into a small bowl. Pour boiling water over top, and cover. Let chiles soak for 1 hour.

Grind toasted cumin and cloves into a powder, and place into a blender. Add ancho chile powder, onion, garlic, oregano, thyme, vinegar, and lime juice. Remove chiles from soaking water, and place into the blender along with 1/3 cup of the soaking liquid. Cover, and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Place beef roast into a mixing bowl, and pour the guajillo chile paste over top. Coat beef on all sides with paste, then cover the bowl with plastic wrap. Marinate in the refrigerator overnight.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

Transfer beef and marinade to a roasting pan, and arrange bay leaves over top. Cover tightly with aluminum foil. Bake in the preheated oven until beef is very tender and easily pulled apart with a fork, about 6 hours. Let stand, covered, at room temperature for 1 hour before discarding the bay leaves and shredding with two forks.

raw_recipe.headline: Barbacoa
raw_recipe.description: A homemade toasted guajillo chile paste seasoned with cumin, clove, and oregano flavors this delicious Mexican pulled beef that's perfect for tortillas.

review.reviewBody: Just wanted to let you know that barbacoa is not a chuck roast; it is beef cheek meat.

This was WONDERFUL. I improvised and cooked it in the slow cooker on high for 6 hours. came out tender and so juicy and flavorful. The only change was that I added 1 small chile de arbol and 1 chile ancho (instead of powder) pepper (roasted just like the guarillo pepper) to the mix and added 6 cloves of garlic and one fresh big Jalapeno pepper to the blender. I seared the meat and then I cooked the onion in the juices before adding it to the blender. I also added about a 2 TBSpn of tomato paste. My Mother always added a little paste to cut the spice for the kids to eat. The Barbacoa is Delicious! My husband loved it and since its a warm day I cooked it in the slow cooker instead of the oven. Thank you for this wonderful recipe :)

Phenomenal! Didn't have ancho chili powder so just used a spicy Mexican chili powder instead. I also added 1 tsp of chipotle chile powder. Cooked in Dutch oven at 300 degrees for 4 hours then shut off the oven and left it in there for another 2 hours. Trimmed the fat and shred with forks. Wasn't too spicy and the kids loved it also. So tender! Definitely a new favorite!

I tried it, and it was pretty good but I made a couple of alterations. I added salt because I was surprised not to see salt in the recipe. I also added a tomato to balance everything out and I also added a head of garlic when I started to cook it. Also, i marinated it for 5 hours, and cooked in a pot instead of the oven, medium heat for 4 hours. I cut up the meat in the medium size chunks so it would cook a bit faster. But it came out pretty good!! I might add more garlic next time. :)

As others have mentioned, the flavor is unnecessarily bland, and here’s why. First, in making the chile sauce there’s no need to soak the peppers for an hour; 20-30 minutes is plenty of time. Second, sauté the onions and garlic in olive oil, season them with a little salt and pepper, and toss in a couple of minced fresh peppers - Fresno, jalapeño, or Serrano - until they’re all soft but not browned. Now blend them, adding the reserved liquid from soaking the peppers a little at a time until you get the consistency you want, save the rest. (I used 2-3x as many peppers as the recipe calls for abd about 1 1/2 cups of water. And, for my money, leave out the apple cider vinegar). Next revision: whether you decide to cook the roast whole or cube it is up to you, but you won’t be able to shred it if you cube it, so think about how you want to serve it. Under any circumstances, don’t marinate it! Season it with salt and oepper, then brown it on all sides in a skillet, Dutch oven, or braising pan, add the sauce, cover tightly and cook at 309-325 degrees Fahrenheit for hours until it’s falling apart tender.

Great recipe for street style tacos, burritos, tamales, pretty much any Mexican main dish. I did use chipotles in adobo instead of the peppers in the recipe, replaced the water with vegetable broth, and added two tablespoons of brown sugar, but other than that I have done this recipe a few times now and it is always a crowd pleaser. It also goes well using pork instead of beef or even 6-8 chicken breasts. Great recipe, highly recommend.

I’ve always used brisket when making this! It’s probably a Texas thing. For the marinade, I also used EVOO, a bit more of the lime juice, chipotle in adobo (instead of guajillo) and lots of chopped cilantro!

I used a pork butt roast (it was just what I had in the freezer) and it was delicious. Wasn't as spicy as I expected so next time I'll add some jalapeño to the marinade. It's surprising to me that there is no salt listed in the recipe. A tsp added to the marinade would enhance the flavors and help infuse those flavors more fully during the marinating process. Great recipe

This recipe is pretty good. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because the meat needs to be browned before roasting, and because the final product didn't have that spiciness I like barbacoa to have. Next time I'll add more chilies.
I cut this recipe in half, and I used chipotle and ancho chiles because that is what I had on hand. Other than that, made as directed and it was a wonderful, filling Cindo de Mayo dinner.
Very good recipe. I used the crock pot after a quick sear on the beef instead. Flavorful and tender.

Followed the recipe as written. I am spice sensitive but did not find this recipe a problem for me. I was VERY disappointed with the lack of flavor. The meat was tender but outside of that, it was nothing like the ones I have had in the past. I guess I just had to high of expectations with the great reviews. The meat was expensive and now I’m trying to figure out how to save this instead of throwing it out! Any ideas, please share…
This is a perfect Crockpot recipe. Don't forget to marinade the roast. I also cut off the fat so when shredding it makes it easy just to plunk out the fat globs but still retain the flavor it adds.
It was fine but not our favorite barbacoa.
The overnight marinating is important to do. My husband loved this dish.
I made this for a pot luck and everyone loved it. I didn't make any substitutions but you may want to hold back on some of the cayenne if you're really sensitive to spicy things.
You can make barbacoa to your liking, I'd prefer chuck roast meat. Is a process cooking it but it is definitely worth it. I love Mexican food. And barbacoa is one of my favs on the food list
I have used this recipe several times, with good results.
